sentences.text: The instant appeal has been filed by the insurance company challenging the award passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/ Additional Sub Court, Tenkasi in MCOP.No.146 of 2012 primarily on the ground of liability.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/ Additional Sub Court, Tenkasi

sentences.text: 2.The Cross Objection has been filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

(A) Factual matrix:
3.According to the injured claimant, while he was travelling as a passenger in a Bolero Jeep owned by the first respondent and driven by the second respondent, the driver of the said vehicle had driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the electrical pole.
In the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.
According to the petitioner, the said Jeep is insured with the third respondent in the claim petition.
The claimant had sought for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
The claimant had further contended that he is aged 69 years and working as a Firm Engineer in K.C.P.Organic Mango Pulp (P) Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

4.The owner and the driver of the Bolero Jeep had remained exparte and the insurer of the said Jeep had filed a counter contending that the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 accident has taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the petitioner and he had no driving licence at the relevant point of time.
They have also questioned the quantum of compensation as prayed for in the claim petition.
Though they have reserved their rights to file an additional evidence, no such additional counter was filed before the Tribunal.

5.The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence, had arrived at a finding that the accident has taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the Bolero Jeep.
The Tribunal further fixed the notional income at Rs.7000/- per month.

In view of 80%
disability, the Tribunal proceeded to apply multiplier method and fixed a sum of Rs.4,20,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income.

A sum of Rs.2,30,715/- was awarded towards medical expenses, Rs.50,000/- was awarded toward loss of amenities, Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.40,000/- towards attender charges, Rs.10,000/- towards extra nourishment and further a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards transport charges.
Totally, a sum of Rs.7,85,715/- was awarded by the Tribunal.
Challenging the liability, the insurance company has filed the appeal.
Seeking enhancement of compensation, the claimant had filed the cross objection.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35

(B)Contentions of the counsels:
6.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant had relied upon Exhibit R1- insurance policy and contended that though it is a private car package policy, the passengers are covered only under the personal accident coverage up to a maximum of Rs.2,00,000/- per person.

Therefore, according to the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, the liability of the insurance company is limited up to the extent of Rs.2,00,000/- with regard to the claim made by the petitioner and the Tribunal without appreciating the said limit, has proceeded to award a sum of Rs.7,85,715/-.

Hence, he prayed for allowing the appeal restricted the liability of the appellant/insurance company to The Branch Manager vs D.Varagunapandian ....1St on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115438325/
3 Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: In a package policy, the liability is unlimited and it is not bound by the terms of the contract.

He had further contended that there is no https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 plea relating to the limited liability either before the Tribunal or in the grounds of appeal filed before this Court.
8.The learned counsel for the first respondent/claimant had further contended that the claimant has produced Exhibit A8- salary certificate.
Without considering the same, the Tribunal had proceeded to fix the notional income as if the claimant is an unskilled person.

He had further contended that the medical board who had investigated the claimant had arrived at a finding that the claimant is suffering from Quadriplegia and therefore, there is 100% functional disability.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded a separate amount under the head of physical disability.
9.The learned counsel for the first respondent had further contended that the Tribunal has not properly appreciated the medical bills or has awarded any amount towards future medical expenses.
Considering the physical disability of the claimant, the attender charges should have been awarded throughout the life time of the claim petitioner.
He sought for enhancement of compensation under the head of pain and suffering and transport expenses.
10.I have considered the submissions made on either side and perused the material records.

of 2024 (C) Discussion:

(i)Liability 11.The primary contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that as per Exhibit R1- policy,
the liability towards a passenger is restricted to Rs.2,00,000/- though it is a package policy.
A perusal of the counter filed by the insurance company before the Tribunal reveals that no such defence has been taken.
The grounds of appeal filed before this Court also does not raise any such ground questioning the liability based upon the terms of the contract.
The insurance official who was examined as RW2, has not deposed about the limits of liability.

12.The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a judgment reported in (2013) 12 SCC 84 (Ramachandra Vs.
Regional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited) while considering the factual plea raised for the first time in the appeal in a motor accident case, in paragraph Nos.24 to 26 has held as follows.

sentences.text: From this legal position it is also equally clear that in the instant matter insofar as the entitlement of the claimant to the compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act is concerned, the right of the claimant is not affected.

However, the respondent/insurance company had filed an appeal in the High Court contending that the order of the Tribunal could not be sustained in law to the extent of liability over and above the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 liability under the Workmens Compensation Act and on this point the contention of the appellant/company has been accepted by the High Court overlooking the more important fact that the Respondent insurer company had neither produced the policy of insurance before the High Court nor led any evidence to establish that as per terms and conditions of policy extra premium had not been paid.
25 . The question, therefore, is whether the amount of compensation could rightly be apportioned between the insurer/insurance company and the insured/owner of the vehicle.

However, the owner of the vehicle had not appeared before the tribunal but the insurance company allowed the matter to be proceeded before the tribunal and when the respondent/insurance company filed an appeal in the High Court, the insured/owner of the vehicle once again failed to appear but the Respondent- Insurance Company did not pursue for his appearance.

The High Court, however, further overlooked that the apportionment of the amount of compensation between the owner of the vehicle and the insurance company was an inter se dispute between insurance company and the insured/owner of the vehicle and, therefore, the order due to non-appearance of the insured/owner of the vehicle could not have been passed to the detriment of the claimant as the claimant in any case is entitled to the amount of compensation determined by the tribunal.

If the insurance company acquiesced with the situation and allowed the proceeding to continue even in absence of the insured/owner of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 the vehicle who has been held liable to pay the amount even though the insured might have been liable to pay higher premium, the consequence of the same obviously will have to be borne by the insurance company and the claimant cannot be made to suffer.
26.

Hence, at the stage of appeal before the High Court, we find no legal justification for the High Court to leave it open to the insurance company to realize the amount of compensation beyond Rs.32,091/- from the insured/owner as the plea of the respondent/insurance company all through was that the claimant is not entitled to any compensation beyond the extent of liability under the Workmens Compensation Act and the respondent/insurance company had not taken the alternative plea either before the tribunal or the High Court that in case the claimant is held entitled to compensation beyond the extent of liability under the Workmens Compensation Act, the same was not payable as no extra premium was paid by the insured/owner under the policy of insurance.

The insurance company had failed to raise any plea before the courts below i.e. either the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal or the High Court and it did not even contend that in case the claimant is entitled to any compensation beyond what was payable under the Workmens Compensation Act, it is the insured owner who was liable to pay as it had no contractual liability since the insured/owner of the vehicle had not paid any extra premium.

Thus, this plea was never put to test or gone into by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal since the insurance company https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 neither took this plea nor adduced any evidence to that effect so as to give a cause to the High Court to accept this plea of the insurance company straight

sentences.text: 13.In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is clear that the insurance company if they have not raised a plea before the Tribunal, they shall not be entitled to raise the same for the appellate forum.
The new plea now raised before this Court is arising out of terms of the insurance policy and it is not a pure question of law.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the appellant is not right in contending that being a pure question of law, the same can be raised before the appellate forum.

14.The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a judgment reported in 2012 (2) TN MAC 637 (SC) (National Insurance Co.Ltd.,Vs. Balakrishnan & another) in paragraph No.19 has held as follows:
19.

entities.text: 2012 (2) TN MAC 637 (SC) (National Insurance Co.Ltd.,Vs. Balakrishnan & another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is extremely important to note here that till 31st December, 2006 the Tariff Advisory Committee and, thereafter, from 1st January, 2007, IRDA functioned as the statutory regulatory authorities and they are entitled to fix the tariff as well as the terms and conditions of the policies by all insurance companies.

The High Court had issued notice to the Tariff Advisory Committee and the IRDA to explain the factual position as regards the liability of the insurance companies in respect of an occupant in a private car under the comprehensive/package https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 policy.

Before the High Court, the Competent Authority of IRDA had stated that on 2nd June, 1986, the Tariff Advisory Committee had issued instructions to all the insurance companies to cover the pillion rider of a scooter/motorcycle under the comprehensive policy and the said position continues to be in vogue till date.
It had also admitted that the comprehensive policy is presently called a package policy.

It is the admitted position, as the decision would show, the earlier circulars dated 18th March, 1978 and 2nd June,
1986 continue to be valid and effective and all insurance companies are bound to pay the compensation in respect of the liability towards an occupant in a car under the comprehensive/package policy irrespective of the terms and conditions contained in the policy.

The competent authority of the IRDA was also examined before the High Court who stated that the circulars dated 18th March, 1978 and 2nd June, 1986 of the Tariff Advisory Committee were incorporated in the Indian Motor Tariff effective from 1st July, 2002 and they continue to be operative and binding on the insurance companies.
Because of the aforesaid factual position, the circulars dated 16th November 2009 and 3rd December, 2009, that have been reproduced hereinabove, were issued.

15.A careful perusal of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court makes it clear that in cases of package policy/ comprehensive policy, irrespective of the terms and conditions contained in the said policy, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 insurance company are bound to pay compensation in respect of the liability towards an occupant in a Car.

Otherwise, there would not be any meaning for the term 'a package policy' if the insurance company proceeds to restrict their liability to a certain amount, thereby depriving the occupants of a private car from getting higher compensation.

6 16.In view of the above said deliberations, there are no merits in the appeal filed by the insurance company.

(ii) Quantum:
17.The learned counsel appearing for the cross objector had prayed for enhancement of compensation on the ground that the Tribunal had erroneously fixed a sum of Rs.7,000/- as notional income ignoring the fact that he is a skilled person.
A perusal of Exhibit P10 reveals that the injured claimant is a diploma holder.
Exhibit P11 reveals that he has undergone a certificate course in the Department of Agriculture, Madras University in Soil Conservation.

At the time of accident,
the petitioner was working in K.C.P. Organic Mango Pulp (P) Ltd.
Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner was aged about 69 years and he was technically qualified person at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal was not right in adopting the notional income of Rs.7000/- which is meant for an unskilled person.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024
18.Considering the age, technical qualification and organization in which the petitioner is working

,
this Court is inclined to fix the notional income at Rs.15,000/- per month.
Exhibit P15 is the disability certificate issued by the District Medical Board assessing the disability of the claimant at 80%.
The Board has found that the claimant is suffering from Quadriplegia, weakness in all four limbs and he is bed ridden.
In view of this medical assessment, the Tribunal was right in applying the multiplier method.
The age of the claimant was 69 years at the time of the accident and therefore, the Tribunal was right in adopting 5 as the multiplier.

Therefore, the compensation that could be awarded under the head of loss of income is Rs. 15,000/- x 12x5 = 9,00,000/-.
19.
The Tribunal has proceeded to disallow the medical bills to the extent of Rs.14,500/- on the ground that they have not been pleaded in the claim petition.
It is settled position of law, no amount of evidence need to be pleaded.
Therefore, the Tribunal was not right in disallowing the claim of Rs.14,500/-.

After adding Rs.14,500/- to Rs.2,30,715/-, the medical expenses can be enhanced to Rs.2,45,215/-.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Cross Objection (MD).No.35 of 2024 20.Considering the fact that the petitioner is bedridden even after five years of the accident
, this Court is inclined to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.
Being a bed-ridden person, the claimant would require help of the attender throughout his life and hence, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head of attender chargers instead of Rs.40,000/-.
The award under the head of pain and suffering is enhanced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
The award under the head of extra nourishment is enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.

The award under the head of transport charges is enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.25,000/-.
21.In view of the above said discussion

, the award of the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:
 Loss of income Rs. 9,00,000.00  Medical expenses Rs. 2,45,215.00

Therefore, the Tribunal was not right in adopting the notional income of Rs.7000/- which is meant for an unskilled person.
In view of this medical assessment, the Tribunal was right in applying the multiplier method.
The age of the claimant was 69 years at the time of the accident and therefore, the Tribunal was right in adopting 5 as the multiplier.
Therefore, the compensation that could be awarded under the head of loss of income is Rs. 15,000/- x 12x5 = 9,00,000/-.
19.
